expected.rationale: Robert Trent Jones's 1950-51 remodel deliberately pinched the fairway landing area to under 30 yards wide at the dogleg-right turn, so the reward for length (cutting the corner) is a landing area too narrow to reliably hit. Accuracy off the tee and into a tightly guarded, three-tier green is what the hole tests, not distance.
sources: The Fried Egg, 'Oakland Hills Country Club (South) Course Review and Rating'
Sports Talk Florida, 'Taming the Monster: A Round at Oakland Hills'
Cybergolf, 'PGA Championship Preview: Oakland Hills (South Course)'

approximations: the parcel's corridor is set wide (38 yds half-width) to give the dogleg room; the actual bend is carved by a rough band and a fairway bunker rather than by a bent centerline, per this validation set's 'carve, not bend' convention
the sharp ~75-degree turn in the final 100 yards is approximated, not surveyed
the pond immediately left of the green and the green's three-tier slope are approximated as a single water-pond piece and a plain small green
